title: Certified Honest Intervals for Transported Treatment Effects near the Overlap Boundary
banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted: the observable frontier claim is only a conditional transfer from an unproved exact-reference expected-objective bound; no faithful bounded repair establishes the promised field theorem.
gap_reasons: The proposal's observable, all-estimator frontier-order honest-length theorem is replaced by a conditional transfer from an unproved exact-reference premise; the core itself disclaims both that premise and the matched minimax/risk result.

The expected-objective premise in thm:frontier-transfer-corollary remains unproved, leaving neither unconditional frontier-order absolute-risk achievability nor frontier-order honest expected length established.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a finite-bit numerical wrapper, conditional honesty, and several precision and work upper bounds, with an explicit open optimality question. D0.5 found that the headline frontier result assumes the unproved exact-reference expected-objective bound; a legal comparator instance can reject every design. The remaining task is the original unconditional graded-estimator achievability and matching frontier proof, including calibrated Gram gates, rejection cost, Taylor bias, and squared weights across arbitrary sample imbalance.
tldr: A total rational procedure estimates the target ATE from a randomized source trial and independent target covariates, using certified finite enclosures. Its outward Taylor-and-moment certificate dominates every compatible latent design and retains target diagonal squared weights and full-interval fallback. Finite-sample population-ATE coverage is at least \(90\%\), uniformly over the frozen law class and legal acquisition kernels. Public acquisition and per-operand precision \(O(\log N)\) yield an expected certificate surcharge at most \(C_{\mathrm{over}}N^{-2}\), \(O(N\log N)\) rational work, \(O(N\log^3N)\) binary work and \(O(N\log N)\) storage. The exact-real frontier-length premise remains conditional. For procedures additionally promising shrinking honest length, a zero-gap rational witness gives the full frontier coefficient in the necessary endpoint precision.
gap: Bias-aware inference requires a valid bias allowance, and verified numerical methods certify fixed instances. Imprecise-data intervals already account for enclosure uncertainty, but the accessible direct-neighbor abstract gives no random transport Gram-gate certificate or expected numerical-overhead theorem.
fill: A total rational wrapper gives pointwise certificate domination, unconditional finite-sample coverage and an \(N^{-2}\) expected overhead bound for the exact-arithmetic Taylor-and-residual reference. Clipping contracts length, and \(N^{-2}\le m^{-1/2}\) absorbs the overhead for every sample-size ratio.
